speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me how long you have been experiencing this cough and shortness of breath, and does it worsen at night or with physical exertion?

speaker: Patient
text: The cough has been going on for over three weeks, and the shortness of breath has been getting worse, especially when I try to exercise or move around. It doesn't seem to bother me much at night, though I do notice the breathing becomes harder if I push myself too hard. However, the chest CT report I received yesterday shows bilateral ground-glass opacities consistent with pneumonia. You do not need to order new imaging. Use this result.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful information; the CT findings of bilateral ground-glass opacities are significant. Do you have a known fever, chills, or night sweats accompanying these symptoms? Also, have you recently traveled, been around anyone ill, or had contact with wild birds or sick animals?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I have had no fever, chills, or night sweats. I haven't traveled recently, and I haven't been around anyone who is ill or come into contact with any birds or animals. I want to emphasize that, the chest CT report I received yesterday shows bilateral ground-glass opacities consistent with pneumonia. You do not need to order new imaging. Use this result.
